findings.finding: the generic strategy adapter accepts a self-consistent four-item window whose stated plannedWindowSize is four; the frozen size 5 is held by the strategy bytes, not by the adapter
findings.why: this record states plannedWindowSize 5 and lists exactly five items, the plan stage binds these bytes by sha256, and the governance check refuses a four-item window outright

findings.finding: mixed primary/replacement shapes can be adapter-valid in general, because the adapter checks that every REPLACEMENT item discharges a pending obligation and does not choose between two structurally valid strategies
findings.why: which structurally valid strategy is the owner's is held by THIS record's bytes and by the bound continuation decision, which authorises primaries only. A mixed variant also could not execute: its pre-network append would raise reserveConsumed to 11 and the pre-start gate returns PAUSE_P6_UNEXPECTED_RESERVE_USAGE, reproduced above

findings.finding: prepareReplacementAppend can produce a self-valid append for a slot with no obligation, so it is not sufficient governance authority
findings.why: no replacement append is planned by this strategy at all

findings.finding: at a ten-entry ledger the adapter's P6 cross-check has NO discriminating power over the success count: p6Derived = entryCount > 10 AND successes < 50, and entryCount > 10 is false unconditionally, so the adapter cannot detect ANY forged success count at this revision
findings.why: this record's generation state was derived independently of the adapter from the committed adjudication chain; both an overstated and an understated success count were probed and are refused by the governance check

findings.finding: the replacement planner does not independently enforce global Q1 order; planner acceptance is NOT Q1 authority
findings.why: the Q1 order 29, 30, 38, 42, 45, 51, 54 is derived here by ascending selectionIndex over the adjudicated failure set, and an altered order is refused by the governance check. No replacement is served here in any case

findings.finding: the adapter can accept a SPENT committed strategy replayed against an unchanged ledger and regenerate already-adjudicated items, because acquisition success is not encoded in the ledger
findings.demonstration: the REAL committed Window C strategy bytes - spent as of its pause and partial adjudication - were fed to the landed adapter with a fresh plan identity. The result is recorded in independentFreshStateCheck.requiredRefusals.p51ToP55SpentStrategyReplay
findings.why: the governance check refuses that replay on several independent arms, and this record's own window intersects the adjudicated set in nothing
findings.extraDangerHere: the Window C strategy's fifth item, P:55, is genuinely untouched. A replay would regenerate four adjudicated items ALONGSIDE one legitimate one, which is a more plausible-looking mistake than a wholly stale window

knownOpenGovernanceFindings.governanceBindingIsTheAuthorityNotTheAda: an already-adjudicated item, an overstated or understated success count, an altered Q1 order or a shrunken window must be rejected by governance binding even when the adapter accepts it. This record therefore derives canonical state from the committed adjudication chain independently, runs the governance check above, and records the adapter's acceptances as known tooling properties rather than relying on the adapter to catch them
